cse-2010-cs-46.approach: Deadlock needs a circular wait. An even process asks $R_i$ then $R_{i+2}$; an odd process asks $R_{n-j}$ then $R_{n-j-2}$. A two-process cycle forms exactly when the odd process holds the resource the even one wants next and wants the one the even one holds.

steps.title: Condition for a cycle
steps.body:
Even $P_i$ holds $R_i$, waits for $R_{i+2}$. Odd $P_j$ holds $R_{n-j}$, waits for $R_{n-j-2}$.

Cycle $\iff n-j=i+2$ (then $n-j-2=i$), i.e.
$$i+j=n-2,\quad i\text{ even},\ j\text{ odd},\ i,j<k.$$
Even + odd is odd, so $n-2$ must be odd $\Rightarrow n$ must be **odd**.

steps.title: Eliminate even n
steps.body: (A) $n=40$ and (C) $n=20$ are even, so $i+j=n-2$ is even — impossible for an even $i$ and an odd $j$. No deadlock.

steps.title: Check the odd cases
steps.body:
(B) $n=21,k=12$: need $i+j=19$ with $i,j\le 11$: $i=8,j=11$ ($R_8$ and $R_{10}$) or $i=10,j=9$ ($R_{10}$ and $R_{12}$). The conditions $i+2<n$ and $j<n$ hold, so both requests are made. **Deadlock possible.**

(D) $n=41,k=19$: need $i+j=39$, but $i,j\le 18$ gives at most $18+17=35<39$. No cycle.

optionAnalysis.reason: $n=40$ is even, so $i+j=38$ cannot have one even and one odd index — no circular wait.
$P_8$ holds $R_8$ and wants $R_{10}$ while $P_{11}$ holds $R_{10}$ and wants $R_8$ — a cycle.
$n=20$ is even — no even/odd pair sums to 18.
$n=41$ needs $i+j=39$, but with $k=19$ the largest even+odd sum is $18+17=35$.

cse-2010-cs-46.shortcut: Need $i+j=n-2$ with $i$ even, $j$ odd and both $<k$: $n$ must be odd and $n-2\le 2k-3$.
pitfalls: Forgetting that the indices must be below $k$ (option D fails only because of $k$).
Looking for cycles between two even processes — both request in increasing index order, so they cannot deadlock with each other.
cse-2010-cs-46.verification: For B, traced $P_8$: requests $R_8$ then $R_{10}$; $P_{11}$: requests $R_{21-11}=R_{10}$ then $R_{8}$ — opposite orders on the same pair.
